method: All 63 expected answers independently recomputed in Python (brute force where possible); all matched. Compared against dev.json for duplicates; none found. Model not run.

changes.issue: Asks for a percent while the mandatory decimal format sentence shows 'ANSWER: 0.25' and forbids the percent sign, so a correct solver could answer 0.44 and fail the 43.75 check
changes.action: Added a sentence to the prompt stating the percent must be a number between 0 and 100; expected answer unchanged

changes.issue: Near-duplicate scenario of g1-18 (40-litre vessel, 25% concentrate, drain and replace with pure) and second mixture task in the same file (g2-09)
changes.action: Replaced with a new hard function-composition equation task (f(x)=2x+3, f(f(x))=f(x)+30, answer 12, verified by brute force)

changes.issue: Exact duplicate of g2-12 (two-digit number, digit sum 11, swap adds 27)
changes.action: Replaced with a new medium task: digit sum of 200 written in base 7 (answer 8, verified)

changes.issue: Base-5 answer: a correct 'ANSWER: 432 (base 5)' or '432_5' is read by the number checker as 5 and fails
changes.action: Wrapped in 'any': number 432 OR a regex accepting a last ANSWER line of 432 with an optional base-5 suffix; tested that 4325, 432.5, 1432, 377 and 'base 6' still fail

notes: Difficulty mix is unchanged; gen_1 and gen_2 have 6-7 easy tasks each, more than the spec's roughly 2-in-10 target, and several are standard textbook items the spec says are near ceiling for the baseline. Not altered in this review.
g3-13 with no ANSWER line at all (truncated reply ending '... in base 5') still fails via the number fallback; left as is to avoid false positives.
